apps.name: Helix
apps.text: A modal text editor with multiple selections and syntax trees built in.

apps.name: micro
apps.text: A terminal text editor with the keys people already know: Ctrl-S saves, Ctrl-Q quits.

apps.name: Kakoune
apps.text: A modal editor where you select first and act second. Runs shell snippets, so it may run other programs.

apps.name: Vim
apps.text: The classic modal editor, with its full runtime of syntax files and plugins.

apps.name: bat
apps.text: cat with syntax highlighting and line numbers. Runs a pager for long files.

apps.name: eza
apps.text: A modern ls: colours, file types, trees and long listings.

apps.name: nnn
apps.text: A tiny, fast file manager. Opens files in other programs.

apps.name: ncdu
apps.text: See what takes the space in a directory tree, and clean it up.

apps.name: fzf
apps.text: A fuzzy finder for files, lines and anything else piped into it.

apps.name: Git
apps.text: Version control for repositories on this machine: init, commit, branch, merge, log and diff. Remotes are not served: git's HTTP and SSH helpers have no box of their own and are refused at their installed paths.

apps.name: tig
apps.text: A text interface for browsing a Git repository's history. Runs git.

apps.name: lazygit
apps.text: A terminal interface for Git: stage, commit, branch and rebase with a few keys. Runs git.

apps.name: age
apps.text: Simple, modern file encryption, offline, to a passphrase or to a recipient key made elsewhere. The age-keygen in its package has no box of its own and is refused at its installed path.

apps.name: minisign
apps.text: Sign files and verify signatures, offline, with tiny Ed25519 keys.

apps.name: FLAC
apps.text: Encode and decode lossless FLAC audio files. The metaflac in its package has no box of its own and is refused at its installed path.

apps.name: LAME
apps.text: Encode audio files to MP3.

apps.name: Geth (dev chain)
apps.text: go-ethereum for local development: geth --dev runs a private chain on this machine with its console. It cannot sync a public network here.

apps.name: Profanity (XMPP, OMEMO)
apps.text: A terminal XMPP chat client with OMEMO end-to-end encryption. Every connection leaves over Nym or Anyone, never direct, so your server never learns your address, but it still sees your account, your contacts and when you talk. Its box allows any server: a market release cannot carry a list of servers yet.

apps.name: Monero wallet (CLI)
apps.text: Monero's command-line wallet. It starts with a public remote node, xmr-node.cakewallet.com:18081, as an untrusted node, so it offers no mining, and logs to its home; name another with --daemon-address. It reaches the node over Nym or Anyone, never direct, so the node never learns your address; it still sees which outputs your wallet asks about. Its box allows any node: a market release cannot carry a list of destinations yet. The daemon and tools in its package have no box of their own and are refused.

apps.name: swayimg
apps.text: An image viewer that opens in its own window: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG and more, with zoom, pan and a slideshow. It reads only files in its own home and has no network at all. It decodes untrusted images with the usual libraries, so a hostile image is held by its box, not by the viewer.

apps.name: Telegram Desktop
apps.text: Telegram's desktop client, in its own window. It reaches Telegram's servers over Anyone, never direct, so they never learn your address. They still see your account's phone number, your contacts, who you talk to and when, and your messages: the desktop app has no secret chats, so nothing it sends is end-to-end encrypted. It runs in its own box, with its own home and no other files.

apps.name: DarkFi wallet (drk)
apps.text: DarkFi's command-line wallet, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0 without its tor and i2p transports. It keeps its keys in its own home and asks a darkfid node over JSON-RPC: a node you run yourself, or a remote node you name, reached over Anyone, never direct. A remote node never learns your address, but it sees which coins your wallet asks about. A full chain does not fit an app's home, so on the live network the node is a remote one.

apps.name: DarkIRC (P2P chat)
apps.text: DarkFi's peer-to-peer IRC daemon, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0 without its tor and i2p transports. It reaches its peers over plain tcp and tls, which leave over Anyone, never direct, so a peer never learns your address. Peers still see the channels you join and when you talk; encrypted channels hide what is said only from those without the channel key.

apps.name: DarkFi node (darkfid), local or dev chain only
apps.text: DarkFi's full node, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0 without its tor and i2p transports. For a local or dev chain only: a mainnet or testnet chain does not fit an app's 16 MiB home. It serves drk's JSON-RPC on 127.0.0.1 inside its own box, and any peer it dials leaves over Anyone, never direct. Its box lets it compile code as it runs (JIT), as wasmer does for each contract and RandomX for its proof of work.

apps.name: KeePassXC
apps.text: A password manager that keeps your passwords in one encrypted file in its own home, offline. Its box has no network at all, so nothing it holds can leave the machine through it. It opens in its own window in the NØNOS frame; copied passwords go to the NØNOS clipboard, and are cleared there when KeePassXC clears them.

apps.name: Mousepad (text editor)
apps.text: A simple text editor in its own window, with tabs, search and replace, syntax highlighting and spell checking. It opens and saves only files in its own home and has no network at all.

apps.name: foot (terminal)
apps.text: A fast Wayland terminal in its own window, running a shell. Its box may start programs, as a terminal starts its shell, and every program it starts is held to the same box: its own home, no network.

apps.name: mpv (media player)
apps.text: A media player in its own window, for the video and audio files in its own home. It draws in software, with no GPU, and has no network at all, so it plays only what is already in its home.

apps.name: SimpleX Chat (terminal)
apps.text: SimpleX Chat v7.0.3 in a terminal: SimpleX's own release binary, not built here, pinned by sha256 and BLAKE3 and checked against SimpleX's signed checksums. It runs in the Debian family's tree with pinned Debian libraries. It reaches SMP servers over Anyone or Nym, never direct, and keeps its database, your profile, contacts and messages, in its own home. That home lasts until the machine powers off: a live session, gone then, until kept homes come.
